title: Groundnut — Irrigation Management and Critical Stages
content:
CRITICAL IRRIGATION STAGES FOR GROUNDNUT:
1. Flowering stage (25-30 DAS): Critical — moisture stress causes flower drop.
2. Pegging stage (40-45 DAS): Very critical — stress reduces pod set.
3. Kernel development (55-65 DAS): Critical — stress reduces pod weight.
4. Pod filling (70-80 DAS): Important — maintain field capacity.

IRRIGATION SCHEDULE:
- Kharif (rainfed): Supplement irrigation at critical stages if rainfall gaps > 15 days.
- Rabi/Summer: Irrigate every 10-12 days. Total 6-8 irrigations.
- Total water requirement: 450-550 mm over crop season.

METHODS:
- Drip irrigation: 60% water saving, 15-20% yield increase. Recommended for Karnataka.
- Furrow irrigation: 200 mm/irrigation per furrow.
- Flood irrigation: 50-60 mm per irrigation.

WATERLOGGING: Groundnut is highly sensitive — waterlogging for >48 hours causes yield loss. Ensure good drainage.

DROUGHT MANAGEMENT:
- Apply 100 kg/ha of sand mulch or paddy straw mulch to conserve soil moisture.
- KNO3 0.5% foliar spray at flowering and pegging if moisture stress.
- Use GPBD-4 or drought-tolerant varieties for rainfed areas.
